title: Bus & Rental
summary: Daily AC tourist buses Kathmandu–Pokhara and Kathmandu–Chitwan, plus private car, jeep, van, microbus, and coach rental from our Thamel desk.
metaTitle: Bus & Rental Nepal | Kathmandu Pokhara & Chitwan
metaDescription: World Touch daily tourist bus Kathmandu to Pokhara and Chitwan, AC sofa seats, and rental cars, jeeps, vans, microbuses, and coaches with driver.
heroAlt: World Touch tourist coach for Kathmandu, Pokhara, and Chitwan routes
overview: World Touch is not only treks and tours — we run and book the road days that connect them. Daily tourist coaches leave Kathmandu in the morning for Pokhara on the Prithvi Highway and for Chitwan (Sauraha) on the Terai highway, with reserved AC seats, sofa-style reclining chairs, and a water bottle when you board.

Pokhara is the lake city and trek gateway most guests know: about 200 km, 7–8 hours beside the Trishuli with meal stops. Chitwan is the jungle contrast — roughly 5–6 hours to Sauraha for safari lodges, often booked after a trek or as part of a Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan loop.

We also arrange rental vehicles with driver from Kathmandu: cars for city and valley days, jeeps for ridge roads and park transfers, vans and microbuses for families and small groups, and full tourist-bus charter when you need a private coach. Tell us dates, passengers, and route — we confirm from the desk, not a random broker on the street.
Everything is booked through the same Thamel team that handles your trek permits and tour guides, so bus seats, Chitwan transfers, and hire vehicles can sit on one itinerary.
history: Whether you are watching the Trishuli gorge open toward Pokhara or dropping from the hills into warm Terai air for Chitwan, these are full travel days — best with a window seat, realistic timing, and a crew that knows the stops.

policies.title: Booking
policies.detail: Reserve by WhatsApp, email, or the contact form. Same-day bus seats are sometimes available before 6:00 if the coach is not full. Rental vehicles need advance notice for availability.

policies.title: Payment
policies.detail: Pay at our Thamel desk, by bank transfer, or in cash on boarding for confirmed bus bookings. Vehicle hire is quoted per day or route — we confirm before you travel.

policies.title: Cancellation
policies.detail: Bus seat changes are free up to 24 hours before departure when we can resell the place. Rental cancellations depend on how close to the start date — we state this clearly when you book.

policies.title: Luggage
policies.detail: One trek duffel and one cabin bag is the usual allowance on tourist buses. Charter and van luggage limits depend on vehicle size — ask when you book.

policies.title: ID
policies.detail: Carry your passport. Crews may note names against the manifest on tourist coaches.

faqs.question: How long is the Kathmandu to Pokhara bus?
faqs.answer: Plan on 7 to 8 hours, including breakfast and lunch stops. Landslides or traffic near Mugling can make it longer.

faqs.question: Do you run a Kathmandu to Chitwan bus?
faqs.answer: Yes. Morning tourist coaches run toward Sauraha (Chitwan) in about 5 to 6 hours with a meal stop. Book both directions through our desk.

faqs.question: Can I combine Pokhara and Chitwan buses?
faqs.answer: Many guests bus Kathmandu–Pokhara for a trek or lake stay, then continue to Chitwan by road or book our multi-day tour. We help sequence dates and seats.

faqs.question: What rental vehicles do you offer?
faqs.answer: Car, jeep, van, microbus, and full tourist-bus charter with driver — for valley days, park transfers, or private group loops. We quote based on route and season.

faqs.question: What is included on the tourist bus?
faqs.answer: Reserved seat, AC cabin, sofa-style seating, and a water bottle on boarding. Meals are at highway stops — you pay locally.

faqs.question: Do you pick up from my hotel?
faqs.answer: Thamel hotels are covered on many morning Kathmandu departures. Outside Thamel, ask us — we will say clearly if you need to reach the bus park.

faqs.question: Is there Wi-Fi on the bus?
faqs.answer: Do not count on it. Mobile data works on much of the highway and drops in the gorges.
